hints.content:
Here is the completed table. 

$x$ | $y$ 
:-: | :-: 
$\redE3$ | $\purpleD{2}$
$\redE5$ | $\purpleD{6}$
$\redE7$ | $\purpleD{10}$

Now, let's try each rule to see whether it works for all $3$ coordinates.

|| **Subtract $1$ from $x$ to get $y$.** ||
$x$ | $y$ | Matches graph?
:-: | :-: | :-:
$\redE{3}$ | $\redE{3}-1=\purpleD{2}$ | Yes
$\redE{5}$ | $\redE{5}-1=\purpleD{4}$ | No
$\redE{7}$ | $\redE{7}-1=\purpleD{6}$ | No

This rule does *not work* for all of the values.

|| **Multiply $x$ by $2$. Then subtract $4$ from the product to get $y$.** ||
$x$ | $y$ | Matches graph?
:-: | :-: | :-:
$\redE{3}$ | $(2 \times \redE{3})-4=\purpleD{2}$ | Yes
$\redE{5}$ | $(2 \times \redE{5})-4=\purpleD{6}$ | Yes
$\redE{7}$ | $(2 \times \redE{7})-4=\purpleD{10}$ | Yes

This rule works for all of the values.

This is the completed table.

$x$ | $y$ 
:-: | :-: 
$3$ | $2$
$5$ | $6$
$7$ | $10$

The rule that describes the relationship between $x$ and $y$ is, "Multiply $x$ by $2$. Then subtract $4$ from the product to get $y$."
